## Model {#sec-model}

The instances, the plans, the rounding of rational and real times, the assumptions on central
flights and the Pareto front, as fixed in §1 of the note. These definitions are the trusted
interface of the formalization: every theorem below is about them.

### Definition 1.1 (instance) {#node-definition-1-1}

::: {.node-badge}
[Lean definition]{.badge .ok}
:::

::: {.node-body}
**Definition 1.1 (instance).** An instance has two *hubs*, $C_I$ (initial) and $C_G$ (goal), and
central cities $1, \dots, n$. Durations are natural numbers. The flight between $C_I$ and $i$ lasts
$d_i$ in either direction, the flight between $i$ and $C_G$ lasts $\bar d_i$, and for every ordered
pair $(i, j)$ of central cities, $i = j$ included, the central flight from $i$ to $j$ lasts
$d_c(i, j)$. No flight joins the two hubs. $\mathrm{dur}(a, b)$ is the duration of the flight from $a$
to $b$. Landing in central city $i$ costs $c_i \in \mathbb N$; landing in a hub is free. There are
$p$ planes and $t$ passengers, all in $C_I$ at time 0. A plane carries at most one passenger. Results
assume $1 \le p \le t$ where they use it.

::: {.node-lean}

:::

**Lean** `ZenoFront.Network.duration` [Lean definition]{.badge .ok}

```lean
/-- The duration of the flight between two locations, if there is one. There is no flight
between two hubs. -/
def Network.duration (N : Network n) : Loc n → Loc n → Option ℕ
  | .ci, .city i => some (N.d i)
  | .city i, .ci => some (N.d i)
  | .cg, .city i => some (N.dbar i)
  | .city i, .cg => some (N.dbar i)
  | .city i, .city j => some (N.dc i j)
  | _, _ => none
```

### Definition 1.2 (plan) {#node-definition-1-2}

::: {.node-badge}
[Lean definition]{.badge .ok}
:::

::: {.node-body}
**Definition 1.2 (plan).** A *leg* is a tuple (origin, destination, departure, arrival, passenger or
none), with natural-number times. A *plan* gives each plane a list of legs. A list of legs is a
*route from $x$ at time $\tau$* if its first leg leaves $x$ no earlier than $\tau$ and each later leg
leaves where the previous one arrived, no earlier than that arrival. The plan is *feasible* if

1. every leg is a flight: its origin and destination are joined by a flight, and its arrival is its
   departure plus the flight's duration;
2. the legs of each plane form a route from $C_I$ at time 0 whose last leg arrives in $C_G$;
3. for every passenger, the legs that carry it form, in some order, a route from $C_I$ at time 0 whose
   last leg arrives in $C_G$.

The *cost* $C$ of a plan is the sum of the landing costs of all its legs that land in a central city.
Its *makespan* $M$ is the latest end of a route, the arrival of its last leg. The *flight time* $F_k$
of plane $k$ is the sum of the durations of its legs. $\mathcal A$ is the set of points $(C, M)$ of
the feasible plans.

*Planes ending anywhere.* In this variant (PDDL problems without plane goals), item 2 only asks for a
route from $C_I$ at time 0, possibly empty; item 3 is unchanged. The makespan is the latest arrival of
a leg (0 for a plane without legs). $\mathcal A'$ is the set of points of the plans of the variant.

::: {.node-lean}

Waiting is implicit: a departure may be later than the preceding arrival, for planes and for
passengers. A leg names at most one passenger, which is the capacity constraint. Boarding and
debarking take no time, several planes may be in a city at once, and a passenger may change planes in
any city.

```lean
/-- A leg is a flight of the network, and lasts exactly the flight's duration. -/
def Flies (N : Network n) (ℓ : Leg n t) : Prop :=
  ∃ τ, N.duration ℓ.src ℓ.dst = some τ ∧ ℓ.arr = ℓ.dep + τ
```

[`lean/ZenoFront/Plan.lean`, lines 106–108](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Plan.lean#L106-L108){.lean-src}

**Lean** `ZenoFront.IsRoute` [Lean definition]{.badge .ok}

```lean
/-- `IsRoute x τ legs`: starting at `x` at time `τ`, each leg leaves where the previous one
arrived (or `x`), no earlier than that arrival (or `τ`). Waiting is allowed. -/
def IsRoute : Loc n → ℕ → List (Leg n t) → Prop
  | _, _, [] => True
  | x, τ, ℓ :: rest => ℓ.src = x ∧ τ ≤ ℓ.dep ∧ IsRoute ℓ.dst ℓ.arr rest
```

[`lean/ZenoFront/Plan.lean`, lines 110–114](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Plan.lean#L110-L114){.lean-src}

```lean
/-- A feasible plane: its legs are flights, they form a route from `C_I` at time `0`, and the
plane ends in `C_G`. -/
structure PlaneFeasible (N : Network n) (legs : List (Leg n t)) : Prop where
  flies : ∀ ℓ ∈ legs, Flies N ℓ
  route : IsRoute .ci 0 legs
  ends : finalLoc .ci legs = .cg
```

```lean
/-- A feasible plan: every plane is feasible, and the legs carrying each passenger form, in some
order, a route from `C_I` at time `0` that ends in `C_G`. -/
structure Feasible (N : Network n) (P : Plan n t p) : Prop where
  planes : ∀ k, PlaneFeasible N (P k)
  pax : ∀ π, ∃ route : List (Leg n t), route.Perm (paxLegs P π) ∧ IsRoute .ci 0 route ∧
    finalLoc .ci route = .cg
```

### Lemma 1.3 (rounding times) {#node-lemma-1-3}

::: {.node-badge}
[machine-checked]{.badge .ok}
:::

::: {.node-body}
**Lemma 1.3 (rounding times).** Let $\mathbb K$ be an ordered ring with a floor function, such as
$\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb R$, and let a plan have departures and arrivals in $\mathbb K$ (and the
instance's integer durations) and satisfy items 1–3 of Definition 1.2. Rounding every time down gives
a feasible plan with natural-number times, the same cost and a makespan at most the original one.
Conversely, a feasible plan with natural-number times, read in $\mathbb K$, satisfies items 1–3 with
the same cost and makespan.

::: {.node-lean}
Lean: [`QFeasible` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/RationalPlans.lean#L102-L106), [`QFeasible.floor` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/RationalPlans.lean#L176-L191), [`qPlanCost_eq` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/RationalPlans.lean#L194-L196), [`planMakespan_floor_le` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/RationalPlans.lean#L224-L241), [`Feasible.toRat` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/RationalPlans.lean#L274-L303)
:::

```{=html}
<details class="node-more"><summary>Proof</summary>
```

theory note, §1.2 · ledger `lem-rounding`

*Proof.* A leg with arrival $a = e + \tau$, $\tau \in \mathbb N$, has $\lfloor a\rfloor = \lfloor e
\rfloor + \tau$, so it stays a flight. Rounding down is monotone, so an inequality $a \le e'$ between
an arrival and the next departure survives it, for planes and for passengers, in the same orders, and
so does $0 \le e$ for the first departure. Locations and passengers do not change, so neither does the
cost, and $\lfloor x\rfloor \le x$ bounds the new makespan by the old one. The converse holds because
$\mathbb N \to \mathbb K$ preserves sums and order. $\square$

```{=html}
</details>
```

```{=html}
<details class="node-more"><summary>Lean statement and source</summary>
```

### Definition 1.4 (assumptions) {#node-definition-1-4}

::: {.node-badge}
[Lean definition]{.badge .ok}
:::

::: {.node-body}
**Definition 1.4 (assumptions).** Each is used only where a result states it.

* (S) symmetry: $\bar d_i = d_i$ for all $i$.
* (A1) central flights are useless: $d_i + d_j \le d_c(i, j)$ for all central $i, j$. This is the
  EvoCOP 2015 assumption (stated there with $>$, under (S)).
* (A1-NS) $\min(d_i + d_j,\ \bar d_i + \bar d_j) \le d_c(i, j)$ for all central $i, j$.
* (AΔ) $\mathrm{dur}(a, b) \le \mathrm{dur}(a, x) + \mathrm{dur}(x, b)$ whenever $a \ne b$ and the
  three flights exist.
* (H) the hub triangles: $d_j \le d_i + d_c(i, j)$ and $d_i \le d_c(i, j) + d_j$ for all central $i, j$.

::: {.node-lean}
Lean: [`Network.A1` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Converse.lean#L34-L35), [`Network.A1NS` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/NonSymmetric.lean#L41-L43), [`Network.ATri` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/TriSegments.lean#L53-L59), [`Network.ATriHub` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/TriSegments.lean#L61-L65)
:::

(H) is (AΔ) on the triangles through $C_I$: $C_I \to i \to j$ against $C_I \to j$, and $i \to j \to
C_I$ against $i \to C_I$. Under (S) these are also the triangles through $C_G$. In (AΔ), the
condition $a \ne b$ leaves the flights $d_c(i, i)$ free.

**Lean** `ZenoFront.Network.A1` [Lean definition]{.badge .ok}

```lean
/-- Assumption (A1): central flights are useless, `dc i j ≥ d i + d j` (under (S)). -/
def Network.A1 (N : Network n) : Prop := ∀ i j, N.d i + N.d j ≤ N.dc i j
```

[`lean/ZenoFront/Converse.lean`, lines 34–35](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Converse.lean#L34-L35){.lean-src}

**Lean** `ZenoFront.Network.A1NS` [Lean definition]{.badge .ok}

```lean
/-- Assumption (A1-NS): a central flight is no shorter than a detour through one of the hubs. -/
def Network.A1NS (N : Network n) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, min (N.d i + N.d j) (N.dbar i + N.dbar j) ≤ N.dc i j
```

```lean
/-- **Assumption (AΔ)**, the triangle inequality for the flights that exist:
`dur(a, b) ≤ dur(a, x) + dur(x, b)` whenever the flights `a–b`, `a–x` and `x–b` exist and
`a ≠ b`. The note's flights join distinct locations; the condition `a ≠ b` leaves the Lean
network's self-loops `dc i i` free (and `a = x` or `x = b` is trivial). -/
def Network.ATri (N : Network n) : Prop :=
  ∀ a x b : Loc n, a ≠ b → ∀ τab τax τxb : ℕ, N.duration a b = some τab →
    N.duration a x = some τax → N.duration x b = some τxb → τab ≤ τax + τxb
```

[`lean/ZenoFront/TriSegments.lean`, lines 53–59](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/TriSegments.lean#L53-L59){.lean-src}

**Lean** `ZenoFront.Network.ATriHub` [Lean definition]{.badge .ok}

```lean
/-- (AΔ) on the triangles through `C_I`: `d_j ≤ d_i + dc i j` (`C_I → i → j` against `C_I → j`)
and `d_i ≤ dc i j + d_j` (`i → j → C_I` against `i → C_I`). Under (S) these are also the
triangles through `C_G`. This is all that Theorem 4.4 and its corollaries use. -/
def Network.ATriHub (N : Network n) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Fin n, N.d j ≤ N.d i + N.dc i j ∧ N.d i ≤ N.dc i j + N.d j
```

### Definition 1.6 (fronts) {#node-definition-1-6}

::: {.node-badge}
[Lean definition]{.badge .ok}
:::

::: {.node-body}
**Definition 1.6 (fronts).** Points (cost, makespan) of $\mathbb N^2$ are ordered componentwise, and
$y$ *weakly dominates* $z$ if $y \le z$. For $\mathcal S \subseteq \mathbb N^2$, $\mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal
S$ is the set of the minimal points of $\mathcal S$: the $z \in \mathcal S$ such that every $y \in
\mathcal S$ with $y \le z$ is $z$. The *front* is $\mathcal F = \mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal A$. A list is the
*Pareto front* of $\mathcal S$ if its points lie in $\mathcal S$, every point of $\mathcal S$ is weakly
dominated by a listed point, and the listed points are pairwise incomparable.

::: {.node-lean}
Lean: [`achievable` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Checker.lean#L51-L53), [`achievableAnywhere` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Bridge.lean#L75-L77), [`IsParetoFront` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Checker.lean#L55-L60)
:::

```{=html}
<details class="node-more"><summary>In the note</summary>
```

```lean
  {x | ∃ P : Plan n t p, Feasible N P ∧ (planCost c P, planMakespan P) = x}
```

**Lean** `ZenoFront.IsParetoFront` [Lean definition]{.badge .ok}

```lean
/-- `F` is the Pareto front of `S` (for the product order on (cost, makespan)): its points are in
`S`, weakly dominate every point of `S`, and are pairwise incomparable. -/
structure IsParetoFront {α : Type*} [PartialOrder α] (S : Set α) (F : List α) : Prop where
  achieved : ∀ x ∈ F, x ∈ S
  dominates : ∀ y ∈ S, ∃ x ∈ F, x ≤ y
  antichain : F.Pairwise fun a b => ¬ a ≤ b ∧ ¬ b ≤ a
```

### Lemma 1.7 (dominating sets) {#node-lemma-1-7}

::: {.node-badge}
[machine-checked]{.badge .ok}
:::

::: {.node-body}
**Lemma 1.7 (dominating sets).** (a) If every point of $\mathcal A$ is weakly dominated by a point of
$\mathcal B$ and every point of $\mathcal B$ by a point of $\mathcal A$, then $\mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal A =
\mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal B$; in particular when $\mathcal B \subseteq \mathcal A$ and every point of
$\mathcal A$ is weakly dominated by a point of $\mathcal B$. (b) A list that is the Pareto front of
$\mathcal S$ lists exactly the points of $\mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal S$.

::: {.node-lean}
Lean: [`minimal_iff_of_dominated` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Achievability.lean#L985-L989), [`minimal_iff_of_subset_of_dominated` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Bridge.lean#L480-L494), [`IsParetoFront.mem_iff_minimal` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Checker.lean#L62-L79)
:::

```{=html}
<details class="node-more"><summary>Proof</summary>
```

theory note, §1.5 · ledger `lem-1-1`

*Proof.* (a) Let $z \in \mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal A$. Some $b \in \mathcal B$ has $b \le z$, and some $a
\in \mathcal A$ has $a \le b$; then $a = z$, so $b = z \in \mathcal B$. If $y \in \mathcal B$ and $y
\le z$, some $a' \in \mathcal A$ has $a' \le y \le z$, so $a' = z$ and $y = z$. Hence $z \in
\mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal B$, and the other inclusion is symmetric. If $\mathcal B \subseteq \mathcal A$,
every point of $\mathcal B$ is dominated by itself in $\mathcal A$. (b) A listed point $x$ lies in
$\mathcal S$; if $y \in \mathcal S$ and $y \le x$, a listed $x' \le y \le x$ exists, so $x' = x$ by
incomparability, and $y = x$. Conversely, for $z \in \mathrm{Min}\,\mathcal S$ some listed $x \le z$ lies
in $\mathcal S$, so $x = z$. $\square$

```{=html}
</details>
```


### Notation {#node-notation}

::: {.node-badge}
[Lean definition]{.badge .ok}
:::

::: {.node-body}
**Notation.** $s = 2t - p$. For multisets of central cities: $Y(i)$ is the multiplicity of $i$, $|Y|$
the size, $\mathrm{supp}\,Y$ the support, $Y + Z$ the sum and $Z \le Y$ inclusion; $c(Y) = \sum_{w \in
Y} c_w$, $\delta(Y) = \sum_{w\in Y} d_w$, $\bar\delta(Y) = \sum_{w \in Y} \bar d_w$, and with $e_i =
\min(d_i, \bar d_i)$, $e(Y) = \sum_{w \in Y} e_w$. A *partition* of $X$ over the $p$ planes is a
family $X_1, \dots, X_p$ of groups, possibly empty, with $\sum_k X_k = X$; its *loads* are the
$\delta(X_k)$. For a weight $w$ on the cities, $G_w[m][T]$ is the least $c(Y)$ over the multisets $Y$
with $|Y| = m$ and $w(Y) \le T$ ($\infty$ if there is none), and $G = G_d$. $d_{\min}$, $d_{\max}$ and
$c_{\min}$ are the least and largest durations and the least cost.

::: {.node-lean}
Lean: [`Instance.s` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Model.lean#L52-L53), [`Groups` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Model.lean#L65-L66), [`size` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Model.lean#L111-L112), [`load` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Model.lean#L70-L72), [`cost` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Model.lean#L74-L75), [`totalCost` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Model.lean#L114-L115), [`Network.emin` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/PlanBounds.lean#L186-L188), [`oneplane` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/OnePlane.lean#L55-L59), [`minOf` ↗](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/lean/ZenoFront/Checker.lean#L83-L85)
